data.title: bn-11g: bind exact SealPack identity into the segment footer
data.description:
Closes the coverage-only pack-trust hole before SealPack default-on (Phase 8 exit gate).

Trust chain: the footer's fixed trailer gains flag bit 0 (SEAL_PACK_IDENTITY, under footer_crc); the extension region gains a 48-byte SealPackIdentity section (kind 3, under ext_crc) carrying identity_kind (hash domain+version), pack_format_version, segment_id and the 32-byte identity = blake3(pack header ++ section directory) — the value open_pack already recomputes and verifies.

Install ordering: SealDriver::seal_consolidated hands finalize() the identity from the VERIFIED parse-back, after write_durable_metered (temp -> fsync -> rename -> dir fsync) returns. Footer is the only installation record; no second marker.

Validation: open/recovery refuse a missing/mismatched/truncated/corrupt/unresolvable named pack and raw-fall-back; a legacy .pidx cannot stand in. A corrupt extension must NOT read as 'no pack named' — that is why the flag lives in the other checksum domain. Legacy footers (flag clear) keep coverage-only trust as documented policy (D-FMT-10).

Please review adversarially: (1) the fail-closed matrix in engine.rs check_named_pack, (2) the ordering argument in driver.rs seal_consolidated docs, (3) the spec 01 §3.3.3 / spec 02 §8.3 interaction, (4) the legacy policy's residual exposure.

Evidence: 788/788 green across mess-log/mess-index/mess-store/mess-cli (36 new); cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean; just fmt-check clean; mess-bench 14/14 floors PASS.
